newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik govt, Islamists complete prisoner exchange.
newsitem.headline: Tajik govt, Islamists complete prisoner exchange.

text.p: Tajikistan's secular government and the Islamic opposition have completed the first stage of a prisoner exchange following a peace deal, U.N. observers said on Sunday.

"The exchange of prisoners and detainees...was successfully completed on July 18-20 with the assistance of the United Nations Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT)," said an UNMOT report obtained by Reuters in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
The statement said the exchange was in line with a protocol signed in tandem with a peace agreement on June 27 which ended a four-year civil war in the former Soviet republic.
The exchange took place near the settlement of Childara, 160 km (100 miles) east of Dushanbe.

"The parties exchanged 48 prisoners of war from both sides, including those detained after February 1997. In addition, opposition field commander Mirzo Zioyev released one more prisoner on humanitarian grounds," the statement said.
"This successful operation is an important confidence-building measure which proves the resolve of both sides to fully implement the protocol signed in Moscow."
Tens of thousands of people were killed in Tajikistan's civil war and many more were forced to flee their homes for safety in neighbouring Afghanistan.
Under the peace deal, signed in Moscow and brokered by Iran, Russia and the United Nations, each side had been supposed to release 50 people in the first batch of prisoner exchanges.
The government says about 2,000 of its servicemen are being held by the opposition. The opposition says up to 600 of its fighters are in government prisons.
